newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian banks Q1 profit grew in line with 1996.
newsitem.headline: Belgian banks Q1 profit grew in line with 1996.

text.p: Profit growth in the Belgian banking sector in the first quarter of 1997 was comparable to that in the whole of 1996, the sector's watchdog the Banking and Finance Commission (CBF) said on Monday.
Net profit in 1996 was 70.50 billion Belgian francs, up 36 percent on 1995.

CBF chairman Jean-Louis Duplat told a news conference on 1996 and early 1997 trends that profit growth was underpinned by non-recurrent revenue from sales of financial instruments and strict cost control.
The balance sheet total of the seven largest banks grew by 12 percent in the first five months of 1997, he said.
This too was comparable with the trend in 1996 when their balance sheets expanded by 12.3 percent. For the sector as a whole, 1996 balance sheet growth was 8.9 percent.

Duplat said this year's growth came on the back of increases in client deposits -- particularly those shorter than one year -- and lending. He noted a slight improvement in consumer credit. New mortgage lending was static, but there was active refinancing of existing mortgages as holders sought to benefit from low market interest rates.
Duplat said the banks' net interest margin - the spread between revenue from lending and interest paid on deposits - had narrowed and now amounted to some 1.7 percent from 2.0 percent.

In 1996, interest income in the sector as a whole grew by 7.4 percent, commission income by 15.8 percent -- helped by buoyant financial markets -- while other income, including trading and the sales of securities, was up 23.6 percent.
The seven largest banks accounted for some 70 percent of total 1996 net income and 62 percent of the sector's balance sheet total.
The top seven banks are: Generale Bank, BBL, Kredietbank, Dexia, Cera, Bacob and ASLK/CGER.
